title: 1.5.39 Cause a ReferenceError on Purpose
description: Break it, read the three parts, say which one solved it, then fix it. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Run the broken code
steps.instructions: The file below has a misspelled name. Run it and read the error message that appears.

steps.title: Record the message
steps.instructions: In a comment, write down the error exactly as it appeared.

steps.title: Say which part solved it
steps.instructions: In a comment, say which of the three parts: the kind, the detail, or the place: actually told you what to change, and why.

steps.title: Fix it
steps.instructions: Correct the spelling so the program prints hello.

requirements.title: The misspelling is gone
requirements.description: No use of the misspelled name remains anywhere in the file. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)

requirements.title: The corrected name is printed
requirements.description: Logs greeting, spelled correctly. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)

requirements.title: The error message is recorded
requirements.description: A comment naming ReferenceError. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)

requirements.title: The useful part is identified
requirements.description: A comment saying which of the three parts solved it. Help: 1.5.38 (Reading an Error Message)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "1.5.39 Cause a ReferenceError on Purpose". The task they were given: The file below has a misspelled name. Run it and read the error message that appears. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
